question: T12 (task-7e6a9ba71ebe6c60): what undo steps does a drag of a Scrolling block's Wave Intensity take, and does a drag let go on its start value take one? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it, made on the desktop (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10, phone 1/2/3/10 and 3/2/5/10, as CAP-T12FOLLOW). Mobile View (the frame 428 wide; D stays on the desktop), select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design, a press on Wave Intensity at 90, then a real drag through one DevTools session: a press on the range at 90, a move to each next value gap ms apart, let go gap ms after the last; a read, Escape (let go) and a read, then Cmd+Z with a read after each, never more Cmd+Z than the plan's own steps (one past them takes back another plan's section). P, G, H, S: 90>120>150>180 at 300, 700, 1100 and 1500 ms. B: 90>120>150>180>150>120>90 at 300 ms, let go on 90; D the same on the desktop; C the same at 1500 ms. J: as S, with the pointer moved 3 px either way every 300 ms between the values (the value stays). N: on the desktop a section with the Scrolling block alone, 90, then 90>120>150>180>150>120>90 at 300 ms, one Cmd+Z. R2 read B D S P H G C and R3 P S B G H D C, two edit sessions; J and N in three more (J, then J and N, then N; R2 holds the first J and N, R3 the second). Nothing saved: every session left by Exit Without Saving.
readsAre: As CAP-T12FOLLOW: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (desktop and phone areas, top and height), the section rows in the view shown, the line (marquee and drawing top and height: the phone line is 30 plus the wave high, the desktop's 34 plus it), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' is the page's own record of the drag: pointerdown, each input and change event of the range and pointerup, in ms from the press.
answer: A drag's values a second or more apart are one undo step each; closer ones are one step. P (values about 420 ms apart) and G (700 to 870 ms): let go on 180 (1/2/8/10, the Text block 8/2/10/10), the first Cmd+Z goes back to 90 (1/2/5/10), the next to the start (1/2/3/10). H (about 1200 ms) and S (1600 ms): each Cmd+Z goes back one value, 150 (1/2/7/10), 120 (1/2/6/10), 90, the start.

A drag let go on its start value takes a step, though no change event fires (inputs: pointerup with no change). B: 90 out to 180 and back to 90 leaves 1/2/4/10 (the Text block 4/2/6/10, the line 120 high), Undo on; Cmd+Z brings back 1/2/5/10 as after the press, then the start. D on the desktop: the drag leaves 1/2/5/26 with the Text block at 5/2/7/10; Cmd+Z brings the Text block back to 3/2/5/10, then the start. C (1500 ms): every value is a step, the last one too: Cmd+Z goes back through 120, 150, 180, 150, 120 and 90 to the start.

J: the pointer moving between values does not join them: the same steps as S. N: with the Scrolling block alone the drag out and back leaves the model as it was, and the let go still takes a step: Undo on, Cmd+Z leaves 1/2/5/26 and turns Redo on.
R2 and R3 read alike in all 68 reads but the first two of B and P, whose Redo was left on by the plan read before them. J and N read alike in both their sessions.

Two reads ours differs in that are not the undo steps: D's Text block ends the drag 5/2/7/10 (it followed the foot down as the drag grew and stayed), and C's step at 150 on the way back holds 1/2/7/10 as on the way out. Not read: where between 870 and 1100 ms the split falls (ours takes 1000, as typing); arrow keys on the range; Item Spacing's and Text Size's ranges. Earlier reads by one DevTools process per move (each with a bring-to-front, moves 250 to 400 ms apart) split the steps unevenly and are not stored.

localGuesses.written: none written before the reads; ours on main takes one step at the change event, none for a drag let go on its start
